title: Watching insertion sort
description:
Print the array after each pass of insertion sort.

```
start:  5 2 4 6 1 3
pass 1: 2 5 4 6 1 3
pass 2: 2 4 5 6 1 3
pass 3: 2 4 5 6 1 3
pass 4: 1 2 4 5 6 3
pass 5: 1 2 3 4 5 6
9 shifts
```
hints: For each `i` from 1, keep `key = v[i]`, shift bigger items right while `j > 0 && v[j - 1] > key`, then put `key` at `v[j]` (lesson 3.01).
Sorted input needs 0 shifts; reversed needs n × (n - 1) / 2.
requirements: Sort a `std::vector<int>` in place, printing after each pass.
Count the shifts (each time an element moves one place right).
Try it on sorted and reversed input and note the counts.
stretch: Do the same for selection sort and count swaps instead.
